summary.headline: UFlex Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38% YoY to Rs 53,972 million and EBITDA rose 92% to Rs 9,198 million, with margin at 17%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 38% YoY to Rs 53,972 million and reported EBITDA rose 92% to Rs 9,198 million, with margin up 480 bps to 17%. Normalized EBITDA (after Rs 825 million forex derivative adjustment) was Rs 8,373 million, up 78%, at a 15.5% margin. Overseas operations (Egypt, Mexico, Nigeria) contributed about 91% of the Rs 4,410 million incremental EBITDA, while India volumes and Aseptic softened. Management guided to 35% growth in FY27 revenue and EBITDA over FY26, while saying Q2 would see some normalization from exceptional Q1 realizations.

financial_highlights.metric: Normalized EBITDA (post Rs 825 mn forex derivative adjustment)

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 580 million, 1.5% margin in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Packaging Films (India)
segments.commentary: Volume 29,323 MT, up 9.1% QoQ but declined YoY against a high Q1 FY26 base affected by industry supply shortage. Converters resumed buying after May-June price normalization.

segments.name: Americas
segments.commentary: Volume 31,724 MT, up 18% YoY, supported by US onshoring push and constrained West Asia/India imports.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Volume 35,653 MT, flat YoY; low-priced imports pressured CPP, CIS BOPET steady. Demand expected to moderate next quarter on seasonal holidays.

segments.name: Middle East and Africa
segments.commentary: Volume 39,486 MT, up 14.9% YoY and 16.5% QoQ; Egypt led growth and Nigeria benefited from export opportunities as customers derisked supply chains.

segments.name: Packaging (Aseptic and flexible)
segments.commentary: Volume down 8.4% YoY to 37,285 MT due to shift to high-margin products in India, Aseptic softness from duty-free Indonesian imports, larger pack-size mix overseas and West Asia consignment delays.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth of about 35% over FY26 (management also cited 30%-plus in places); management said it normally avoids guidance.
Q2 expected to see some normalization from exceptionally strong Q1 realizations; management asked investors to benchmark YoY, not QoQ.
Expects FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14%-plus; said margins could be better if geopolitical conditions hold.
Debt-EBITDA targeted at about 3x in FY28 and below 3x by FY29; interest cost expected to fall by about 1% over the next year.
Volume to roughly double over three years to FY29 as Egypt Aseptic, Noida recycling and Mexico WPP ramp; FY26-FY29 CAGR indicated at least 10%, to be confirmed by IR.

Egypt Aseptic (12 billion packs) expected commissioning in H1 FY27, targeting around 30% utilization in year one annualized (about 2 billion packs in FY27 if started 1 October) and 60-70% in year two.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex Rs 4,782 million: Egypt Aseptic Rs 1,236 mn, Mexico WPP bags Rs 205 mn, Noida Sector 155 recycling Rs 320 mn, Dharwad BOPP line Rs 215 mn.
Noida Sector 155 recycling plant (39,000 MT per annum) commissioned 30 April 2026; capex about USD 30-32 million, no further capex planned.
Mexico 80-million-unit WPP bags plant commissioned 31 July 2026; capex about USD 54 million.
Egypt Aseptic greenfield (12 billion packs): over USD 100 million spent, about USD 15 million remaining; commissioning H1 FY27.
Dharwad BOPP brownfield: USD 10 million spent, about USD 50+ million planned over FY27-FY28. Remaining new capex about USD 80-100 million; management says FY27 capex cycle about 75% complete.
Domestic utilization about 70-73%; specialty films (metallizer, ultra-high barrier) utilized about 30-40%. India Aseptic installed capacity about 24 billion packs.
demand_pricing: BOPP prices up about 25-32% and BOPET up about 30-35% from February 2026 (pre West Asia war) levels, per management.
Management said raw material prices rose but less than finished goods, and prices now appear to be normalizing; prices described as stable at current levels while the West Asia crisis persists.
Overseas selling prices said to be about 2.5x India prices; overseas margins higher because pass-through is easier.
Aseptic faces duty-free imports from Indonesia under India trade treaty at aggressive prices; management says value realization improved via shift to value-added films.
Management said it carries little inventory, so Q1 realizations were passed through to customers; customers prefer UFlex's integrated, local supply for security of supply.

qa_highlights.question: How are price realizations and raw material trends shaping up in India and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: BOPP prices up 25-32% and BOPET up 30-35% since February 2026; raw material costs rose less than finished goods prices, which are normalizing.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 margin and growth sustainable for full-year FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing 2-3 years of capex; FY27 guided to about 35% revenue and EBITDA growth over FY26, with FY27 EBITDA margin about 14%-plus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalization expected in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined QoQ benchmarking; said Q2 will normalize from exceptional Q1 realization but growth remains about 35% YoY, with shipment timing risk around West Asia.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15.5% normalized margin sustainable and how much currency impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Forex impact about Rs 70 crore in the quarter (Rs 825 mn per the prepared remarks); management said margins are sustainable over next 3 years, not just FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for surplus cash: debt reduction vs capex vs shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash to go to debt reduction; leverage to fall to about 3x in FY28. No buyback planned; management prefers wealth creation via growth. 60-70% of future capex to value-added products.

qa_highlights.question: Interest rate and rating outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Rated AA by CRISIL and India Ratings; interest cost fell 0.3-0.4% this quarter and management targets a further 1% reduction in the next year.

risks_watch: Egypt Aseptic (12 billion packs) commissioning slipping beyond H1 FY27; management flagged a possible 1-2 week slip and about 2 billion packs in FY27 assumes a 1 October start
Q2 normalization after exceptional Q1 realizations; management declined QoQ benchmarking and flagged shipment timing risk from West Asia and Bab-el-Mandeb disruptions
Sustainability of pricing: BOPP up 25-32% and BOPET up 30-35% since February 2026; management said prices could correct if the West Asia crisis eases
Aseptic pressure from duty-free Indonesian imports under the India trade treaty; Aseptic volumes down 8.4% YoY company-wide and management expects recovery only from Q3

Guidance inconsistency on the call: 35% vs 30%-plus growth, FY27 EBITDA margin of about 14%-plus, and the 15.5% normalized margin treated as sustainable over three years; Q1 forex impact of Rs 825 mn (about Rs 70 crore per the Q&A)

Debt-EBITDA reduction from about 4.5x to about 3.5x, with a target of about 3x in FY28; interest cost cut of about 1% targeted over the next year; FY26-FY29 CAGR of at least 10% still to be confirmed by IR
key_quotes: Whatever numbers we have achieved in Q1, they are very much sustainable.
Generally, we should not give guidance because guidance in today's market scenario is very difficult.
We are derisking our top-line model in such a way that where we are present at least 75% of our turnover should come from near to our customer policy, that is what we are adopting.
I can quote 10% or something, but that will be misleading, so what I'll request is for Surajit to share the number with you once we have the calculations.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on Q1 delivery and on FY27 growth of about 35%, and repeatedly stressed that margins are sustainable for three years. It was evasive on quarterly benchmarking, declining QoQ normalization guidance and pointing investors to YoY comparisons, and it did not give a firm FY29 CAGR, deferring to IR.

growth.why: Management guides ~35% FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth over FY26 with Egypt Aseptic, Noida recycling and Mexico WPP ramping and volume targeted to double by FY29, though Q2 normalizes from exceptional Q1 realizations and India packaging volumes fell 8.4% YoY.
